result:
Posts can now be scheduled with an optional "Publish at" date and time, and `pnpm typecheck` passes. I didn't boot the app or exercise any of the endpoints.

- **Column and migration:** `posts` has a nullable `published_at` text column. I wrote the migration by hand (`db/migrations/20261018120000_scheduled_posts.sql`) and added its journal entry. I did not regenerate the Drizzle snapshot, so you may want to run `void db generate`.
- **Validation:** `publishAt` is optional on create and edit. Absent, `null` or empty means "publish now". A value like `next tuesday` is rejected with the error on `publishAt`, and nothing is saved. Valid values are stored as UTC ISO strings. On edit, leaving `publishAt` out clears the date rather than keeping the old one, following the contract's "absent means publish now".
- **Visibility:** a post counts as public when `published_at` is `NULL` or already past, so nothing has to run when the time arrives. This is checked on the posts list, search and `GET /posts/:id`. Authors also see their own scheduled posts; everyone else gets a 404 on the page. Every post now carries `publishedAt`.
- **Forms and pages:** the create and edit forms have a datetime-local "Publish at (UTC)" input. The list and the post page show a "Scheduled for …" note on posts that haven't gone live yet.

The main changes are in `lib/posts.ts`, `lib/validators.ts`, `pages/posts/index.server.ts` and `pages/posts/[id].server.ts`.
